hypothesis: H3 (variation practice): blocked practice looks better during acquisition but interleaved practice wins retention and transfer, because drilling one passage at a time overwrites the shared motif weights the other passages rely on (contextual interference; the Shea & Morgan 1979 crossover, in silico).

conclusion.summary: Acquisition: blocked 0.801 > interleaved 0.769 (Holm p=0.0064). Retention: interleaved 0.896 > blocked 0.825 (Holm p=1.2e-05). Transfer: interleaved 0.750 > blocked 0.637 (Holm p=0.0064). Full Shea-Morgan crossover: blocked practice was fool's progress — it looked better while practicing and lost at test.

viz.story: Blocked drilling of one passage at a time rides the shared motif weights to fast visible progress, then each new passage overwrites them; interleaving forces the weights to serve all passages at once — worse practice scores, better musician.
